why: Held at unsure on review: the crevasse and moat come from snippets of the report round 10 already held (researcher: Parties descend onto the Vesper Glacier, cross it to the face with a moat in late season and a crevasse noted, using ice axe, rope and harness.)
The descent crosses the Isella Glacier along a rock and moraine walkway, but no page I could read says whether crevasses or roping apply there.

Held at unsure on review: a Bailey Range traverse page that does not describe Pulitzer itself (researcher: The peak is reached only by the Bailey Range high route, where mid-July to mid-August parties carried strap-on crampons for snowfields, and Wikipedia notes an unnamed small glacier on its north slope.)

Held at unsure on review: one early-June day; RULE.md counts early-season snow as no, so it does not show snow through the season (researcher: A June trip report on Rock Mountain found continuous snow from about 4,800 ft, and June is inside this route's stated season, though July-Sep may be bare.)
The only Tailgunner reports are on sites that refuse access, so no readable page settles whether the line is snow-free in its normal season.
